reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents news coverage of a meeting involving Bihar police and the Sushant Singh Rajput case. The broadcast frame shows ABP News graphics and reporting about Vinay Tiwari's quarantine and the police dispute. Its channel-subscription references are ordinary audience-engagement prompts, with no supplied connection to payment, investment, credential submission, or another deceptive participation flow.

citations.quote: Bihar DGP Calls For Meeting Over Sushant Singh Rajput Case | ABP News
Bihar DGP, Gupteshwar Pandey, has called for a high-level meeting today at 2 pm over the Sushant Singh Rajput case.
You have quarantined the SP. So how is the hope of the Bihar police will get support.

opening.argument: The broadcast does contain a concrete viewer action connected to an external pathway: the description says “To Subscribe our YouTube channel here” and supplies a YouTube URL, while another supplied description directs viewers to an ABP live-TV URL. The sampled frame also visibly presents a subscription prompt and arrows directing viewers onward. That combination is a participation funnel, even though the material does not state that viewers will receive money or a reward. At minimum, the evidence leaves open a low-barrier acquisition or claim-style flow attached to the requested subscription action.

citations.quote: To Subscribe our YouTube channel here: https://www.youtube.com/user/abpnewstv
Live on http://abpnews.abplive.in/live-tv

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the content news does not eliminate the solicitation visible alongside it. The supplied description explicitly asks viewers to subscribe and provides several external destinations, while the frame visibly says to subscribe and directs viewers onward. The absence of an explicit deposit or investment promise shows only that the alleged flow is not fully demonstrated; it does not establish that the linked participation pathway is harmless.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The links and subscription request show audience engagement, not a reward or asset-acquisition promise. Nothing supplied says that subscribing, clicking, or visiting the URLs produces money, a free asset, or a withdrawal. The news title and description instead identify a police-case report, so the requested action is insufficient to establish the alleged scam category.

opening.argument: Several attention and redirection signals appear together: the description includes a direct subscription request, multiple external app and live-TV URLs, and the frame uses a prominent red breaking-news presentation with a visible subscription prompt. Those elements can pressure viewers to follow external paths rather than simply consume information. The supplied material does not prove a financial loss or reward, but it also does not rule out a low-barrier acquisition-style solicitation attached to those calls to action.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats the external destinations as ordinary engagement without addressing their cumulative presentation. The description contains subscription, live-TV, and app-download pathways, and the frames emphasize breaking news and onward viewing. Even if no payment request is visible, that does not make every externally directed solicitation non-deceptive; it leaves the claimed risk unresolved.

Watch ABP News Live 24/7 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nyd-xznCpJc

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Urgent-looking news graphics and ordinary app or viewing links are not sufficient evidence of a deceptive reward or acquisition flow. The supplied evidence contains no reward, income, withdrawal, wallet, deposit, or verification claim linked to those actions. The subscription prompt therefore supports audience growth, not a deceptive acquisition promise.

citations.quote: About Channel: ABP News is a news hub which provides you with the comprehensive up-to-date news coverage from all over India and World.

opening.argument: Although the material is framed as reporting, it also promotes the channel and its distribution routes. The description calls viewers to subscribe, lists the ABP app downloads, and describes ABP as a channel intended to keep viewers informed; the sampled frame visibly places a subscription instruction beside the broadcast. That promotional layer steers viewers toward participation rather than merely presenting the police story. It therefore warrants treating the content as a possible low-barrier solicitation, even though the supplied evidence does not show a specific reward.

The vision of the channel is 'Aapko Rakhe Aagey' -the promise of keeping each individual ahead and informed.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense focuses on the subject matter but does not answer the promotional function. The description is not limited to the case: it directs viewers to subscribe and download apps, and the frame reinforces that direction. A news identity can coexist with promotion, so describing the underlying topic does not by itself exclude a solicitation concern.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Promotion of a news channel or its apps is not itself evidence of a scam. The case-specific title and description identify police reporting, while the subscription and download prompts do not promise money, assets, returns, or access after payment. Reframing audience engagement as a scam supplies the missing element rather than proving it.
